Key Research Thinking Patterns: Weakly Supervised Generative Anomaly Detection: Leveraging generative models to learn healthy data distributions and identify anomalies without pixel-level labels, reducing annotation burden in medical imaging. (e.g., Using Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models with classifier guidance to transform diseased CT images to healthy-like states for pancreatic tumor segmentation, achieving a Dice score of 0.320.)

Cryptographic Integrity Verification via Polynomial Proxies: Ensuring computation integrity in distributed systems by mapping neural network operations to polynomial commitments that can be verified without revealing underlying data. (e.g., Developing the ProxyZKP framework using two-stage multivariate polynomial decomposition and Kate Polynomial Commitment to achieve proof generation times 30–50% faster than zk-SNARKs while mitigating gradient inversion attacks.)

Entropy-Driven Routing Optimization: Enhancing the interpretability and efficiency of hierarchical neural architectures by incorporating information-theoretic measures into the routing mechanisms. (e.g., Proposing Entropy-Adjusted Dynamic Routing (EADR) and variance-based agreement indicators in capsule networks to reduce computational load and improve accuracy on CIFAR-10 and SVHN datasets.)

Systematic Critical Synthesis of Generative AI Risks: Employing rigorous literature review methodologies to map the evolution of synthetic media generation and identify gaps in detection robustness and ethical governance. (e.g., Conducting a PRISMA 2020 systematic review to analyze deepfake generation techniques from GANs to diffusion models and evaluate detection effectiveness against cross-modal adversarial attacks.)
Summary Description: Samuel Cheng is a researcher specializing in the intersection of medical image analysis, privacy-preserving machine learning, and neural network interpretability. His work focuses on developing weakly supervised diffusion models for pancreatic cancer diagnostics, eliminating the need for extensive pixel-level annotations. He pioneers cryptographic frameworks like ProxyZKP to secure decentralized federated learning, ensuring data privacy and computation integrity in multi-institutional healthcare settings. Additionally, he advances capsule network architectures through entropy-adjusted dynamic routing to improve model interpretability and efficiency. His research extends to digital forensics, where he systematically evaluates deepfake detection methods against state-of-the-art generative AI, contributing to the development of robust ethical and regulatory frameworks for synthetic media. His methodologies combine advanced generative AI, zero-knowledge proofs, and information theory to address critical challenges in secure, interpretable, and clinically applicable AI systems.
